Expressionist oil painting in the style of Edvard Munch: a dark room at night, swallowed by blue black shadow, lit only by a large computer monitor showing Claude Code in a terminal  pale text, code diffs, blinking cursor. The monitor glows as an unnaturally luminous rectangle, cold light spilling across the desk, warping the room into long nervous curves. A solitary programmer sits from behind, hunched, silhouette dissolving into darkness. Walls bend inward toward the screen; cables twist like veins; terminal text grows illegible at edges, merging with Munch brushstrokes. Palette: midnight blue, bruised violet, charcoal black, pale cyan white, with accents of burnt orange and red. Thick visible paint, wavering contours, raw texture, psychological tension, loneliness, obsession, ecstatic dread  the screen as a modern moon or doorway into the unknowable. No cyberpunk, no neon, no photorealism; unmistakably late 19th century expressionism applied to a contemporary coding scene. --chaos 75 --profile mlgq83s --stylize 750 --weird 1091 --v 8.2

There is no such thing as liberalism - or progressivism, etc.

There is only conservatism. No other political philosophy actually exists; by the political analogue of Gresham's Law, conservatism has driven every other idea out of circulation.

There might be, and should be, anti-conservatism; but it does not yet exist. What would it be? In order to answer that question, it is necessary and sufficient to characterize conservatism. Fortunately, this can be done very concisely.

Conservatism consists of exactly one proposition, to wit:

*There must be in-groups whom the law protects but does not bind, alongside out-groups whom the law binds but does not protect.*

There is nothing more or else to it, and there never has been, in any place or time.
